requirements.businessContext: Admin-side lifecycle management of team accounts inside a league. Covers single-team CRUD (create / edit / delete), CSV/XLSX bulk replace of the roster, group A/B assignment for TVT, and the implicit force-password-reset behaviour that fires whenever an admin (re)sets a team's password. Scoped to admin operations only; the team-side self-service wizard lives in module 04. Cross-league uniqueness of `teamLoginId` (DB unique index `teams_login_id_global_unique`) is the single most important invariant enforced across every write path here.

userStories.soThat: the admin-issued password is never the long-term credential and the team controls its own access

userStories.soThat: I can drop a withdrawn or duplicate team without leaving orphan rows in the database

userStories.iWant: to select multiple teams in the admin dashboard and delete them in one action
userStories.soThat: I can clean up several teams at once without clicking through each row individually

userStories.iWant: to upload an Excel file containing the full team roster and have the system replace the existing non-ghost teams in one shot
userStories.soThat: I can recover from a corrupted roster or import a pre-built season setup quickly

userStories.iWant: the bulk-upload endpoint to validate every row before touching the database
userStories.soThat: a single bad row aborts the whole upload and I am never left with a half-imported roster

businessRules.rule: All team-management endpoints under /api/admin/[leagueId]/* require an authenticated admin or superadmin session AND the caller must have a leagueAdmins row for that leagueId (superadmin bypass excepted); failure returns HTTP 403 Forbidden.
An admin (non-superadmin) cannot operate on a league whose `isActive` flag is false — getAuthorizedLeagueId returns null and the route responds 403.

Create-team requires teamLoginId, teamName, password, player1Name, player1FplId, player2Name, player2FplId — group is optional. Missing any required field returns 400 with `"All fields except group are required"`.
teamLoginId on create and update must match the regex /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,30}$/ — 3 to 30 characters of letters, digits, underscore, or hyphen. Anything else returns 400.

teamLoginId is globally unique across all leagues (DB index `teams_login_id_global_unique`). Create-team rejects any login ID that already exists in any league with 400 `"Team ID already exists globally"`.
Update-team rejects a new login ID that conflicts with any team other than the one being edited (compares conflict row id !== teamId) with 400 `"Team ID already exists globally"`.

If a `group` value is supplied to create-team or update-team it must be exactly `"A"` or `"B"`, otherwise 400 `"Group must be either A or B"`. (Update-team skips this check entirely for leagues whose format is `auction`.)

Team name uniqueness within a league is enforced case-insensitively AND whitespace-insensitively: LOWER(REPLACE(name,' ','')) must not already exist for the same leagueId. Conflict returns 400 `"Team name already exists in this league"`.

On create-team, if group A or B is supplied but no `groups` row exists for that leagueId+name pairing the endpoint auto-creates one with `groupType="pl"`. Same behaviour on update-team and assign-groups.
Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes with cost factor 10 on every write path (create, update, bulk upload). Plaintext is never persisted.
Newly created teams (via either create-team or bulk-upload-teams) are persisted with `mustChangePassword=true` so first login forces a password change.

Update-team treats `password` as optional; only when the supplied value is non-empty and not whitespace-only does it rewrite the hash and set `mustChangePassword=true`. This is the de-facto admin-force-password-reset flow.
Update-team treats players as optional — each player block is updated only when teamId+name+fplId are all present; missing player blocks leave existing player rows untouched.
Update-team is a no-op for groups when the league format is `auction` — the `groupId` column is not touched even if the request body carries a `group` value.
Update-team passing `group="Unassigned"` clears the team's groupId to null (for non-auction leagues).
Update-team rejects updates to teams that don't exist in the authorized league with 404 `"Team not found"` (prevents cross-league hijacking).

Delete-team is transactional: in one DB transaction it removes gameweekCaptains for the team's players, audit logs scoped to the teamId, results for the teamId, fixtures where the team is home or away, the players themselves, and finally the team row. Any failure rolls the entire delete back.
Delete-team rejects deletion of teams that don't belong to the authorized league (404 `"Team not found"`).
Delete-team and update-team both invalidate the league page cache (`invalidateLeaguePageCache(leagueId)`) on success so the public-facing standings/fixtures pages re-render with the new state.
Bulk-upload-teams refuses any league whose format is `auction` with 400 `"Bulk team upload is not available for auction leagues."` Auction has its own onboarding flow (covered by modules 10/13).
Bulk-upload-teams accepts at most 200 rows per request (`rows.length > 200` returns 400 `"Too many rows. Maximum 200 teams per upload."`).
Bulk-upload-teams rejects an empty/non-array `teams` payload with 400 `"No team rows provided"`.

Bulk-upload row validation: each row must have a non-empty teamLoginId, teamName, password, player1Name, player1FplId, player2Name, player2FplId. The `abbreviation` column is accepted but ignored (legacy).

create-team requires the password field non-empty AND of length >= 4. Shorter or missing passwords return HTTP 400. This minimum matches bulk-upload-teams (BR-TEAM-046) so single-team and bulk-import paths cannot diverge.
Bulk-upload requires both players' FPL IDs to be all-digits (`/^\d+$/`), trimmed before testing.

Bulk-upload de-duplicates within the file itself: a teamLoginId that appears twice (case-insensitive) or a teamName that appears twice (whitespace+case-insensitive) is rejected per the second occurrence row.
Bulk-upload validates the `group` column to be exactly `"A"`, `"B"`, or empty; anything else is a row-level error.
Bulk-upload runs every row through validation first; if any row produces an error the endpoint returns 400 with the full `details` array and the database is not modified.
Bulk-upload checks each candidate teamLoginId against rows in OTHER leagues; if any conflict is found it returns 400 `"Some teamLoginIds are already used in other leagues"` without touching the DB.

Once validation passes, bulk-upload wipes ALL non-ghost teams from the target league (cascade-deletes players, fixtures, results, chip plays, captains via FK cascades) before inserting the new roster.
Bulk-upload preserves ghost teams (`isGhost=true`) — they are never deleted by the wipe step. (Ghost teams exist only in Triple Crown for bye fixtures.)

When an admin creates a team via create-team OR bulk-upload-teams (i.e., the admin supplies team name + both players themselves), the inserted team row has isProfileComplete=true. The team-side setup wizard is therefore skipped on first login. Both admin entry points produce identical onboarding state.
Assign-groups requires a non-empty `assignments` array, where every element has `group` exactly `"A"` or `"B"`. Invalid group on any element fails the whole request with 400.

Assign-groups always ensures both groups A and B exist for the league before processing the assignments, creating them with `groupType="pl"` if missing — even if the caller only asked to assign to one of them.

Assign-groups skips any assignment whose teamId is not in the authorized league (records a per-team error string in the `errors[]` response field, continues with the rest, and returns 200 with `updated` count).
Assign-groups updates `teams.updatedAt` to the current Date on every group write so the dashboard cache reflects the change.

GET /api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team returns all non-ghost teams in the league with their players, group name (or `"Unassigned"` when groupId is null), `needsPasswordChange` flag, `isProfileComplete` flag, and PL-club ownership info.

GET /api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team applies the PL Club Auction rename: a team that owns a PL club via `auctionClubOwnership` is returned with `name` = club's full PL name (e.g. "Liverpool") while `rawName` preserves the original team name.
GET /api/admin/[leagueId]/assign-groups returns every team in the league except ghost teams, each labelled with its group's name.

Admin dashboard bulk-delete flow fires N independent DELETE requests sequentially against /delete-team (one per selected team) and reports partial success/failure counts to the user. // CODE-CONFIRMED: may be a defect — confirm with product owner: there is no server-side transaction across the N deletes, so a mid-flight network failure leaves the roster in a partially-deleted state.
Bulk-upload-teams is flagged @deprecated in source — the admin UI no longer renders a Teams upload tab and the endpoint is retained for backwards compatibility with external scripts only.

Delete-team refuses (HTTP 400) to delete a team whose `isGhost===true` with the exact error message `"Cannot delete a ghost team (Triple Crown bye placeholder). Ghost teams are managed automatically by cup group generation."`; non-ghost team deletions proceed normally through the existing transactional cascade. The guard runs immediately after the league-ownership 404 check and before any rows are touched, so the ghost team row and its bye fixtures remain intact.

update-team rejects (400) any edit where existingTeam[0].isGhost === true with the same error string used by delete-team. Ghost teams are managed automatically by cup-group generation and must not be edited by admins. Non-ghost team updates proceed normally through the existing rename / login-id / password / group flow.
The team's owning league is established at create-team and never changes — neither update-team nor bulk-upload exposes a `leagueId` parameter to move a team between leagues.
Update-team uses the HTTP PUT verb (not POST) — admin UI must call `fetch(..., { method: 'PUT' })`. All other team-management endpoints use POST (or DELETE for delete-team).

bulk-upload-teams requires every row's password to be a string of length >= 4. Rows below that minimum are rejected per-row and the whole upload aborts. Same minimum as create-team (BR-TEAM-024) and update-team (BR-TEAM-029).

Cup-typed groups (`groupType="cup"`, used by Triple Crown) are not touched by any module-3 endpoint — assign-groups, create-team, update-team and bulk-upload only create/use groups with `groupType="pl"`.

create-team has a pre-INSERT uniqueness check on teamLoginId, plus a catch block that inspects the DB error cause chain for SQLite/libsql UNIQUE-constraint failures on the teams_login_id_global_unique index. On match it returns HTTP 400 'Team ID already exists globally'. This closes the TOCTOU race where two concurrent requests with the same teamLoginId both pass the pre-check.

Create-team's response payload includes the newly created team's id, teamLoginId, name and group (the literal `group` field the request body supplied, or null) — the raw bcrypt hash is never returned.

defects.title: create-team and update-team accept passwords below 4 chars while bulk-upload-teams rejects them
defects.description: src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team/route.ts:31-44 validates only that `password` is truthy (non-empty), and src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/update-team/route.ts:119-123 only checks `password.trim() !== ''`. Neither imposes a minimum length. By contrast src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/bulk-upload-teams/route.ts:96-98 rejects any row with `String(r.password).length < 4`. The same logical operation ("set this team's password") has divergent guardrails across entry points.
defects.expectedBehaviour: A single shared password-length constraint (e.g. minimum 4 characters) enforced consistently across create-team, update-team and bulk-upload-teams — and ideally aligned with the team-side change-password endpoint in module 01/04.
defects.actualBehaviour: An admin using the single-team Create or Edit forms can set a team's password to a single character; an admin using bulk upload cannot. This makes single-team-created accounts trivially brute-forceable while bulk-imported accounts are not.
defects.notes: Fix options: (a) add a shared `validatePassword(pwd)` helper in src/lib/auth or src/lib/validation and call from all three endpoints; (b) bump bcrypt cost factor while you're there. Risk of fix: legacy admin scripts that POST short passwords to /create-team would start 400-ing — communicate the rule before shipping. [DEV] Self-verified: surgical edits added the same 4-char min check used by bulk-upload-teams. [QA] Re-run TC-TEAM-073 + TC-TEAM-074 — both now expect 400. [BA] BR-TEAM-024 + BR-TEAM-046 + AC-TEAM-030 + AC-TEAM-054 now describe a uniform 4-char min across all three entry points. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-26 — BR-TEAM-024 + BR-TEAM-046 + AC-TEAM-030 + AC-TEAM-054 updated.
defects.resolution: Added 4-char minimum password validation to both create-team (src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team/route.ts:38-44) and update-team (src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/update-team/route.ts:121-127). Both now reject with 400 "Password must be at least 4 characters" when password is shorter than 4 chars. Aligns the single-team admin paths with the bulk-upload-teams import path (route.ts:96-98) so the same logical operation has uniform guardrails across entry points.

defects.title: create-team leaves isProfileComplete=false while bulk-upload-teams sets it to true
defects.description: src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team/route.ts:97-105 inserts the team without setting isProfileComplete, so the schema default (false at src/lib/db/schema.ts:134) takes effect. src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/bulk-upload-teams/route.ts:170-180 inserts with `isProfileComplete: true`. The two admin entry points produce teams in different onboarding states despite providing the same data (team name + 2 players).
defects.expectedBehaviour: Both admin-side write paths should agree on whether an admin-supplied team is considered profile-complete. Either (a) both set `true` (since the admin already supplied a name and both players, the wizard adds no information) or (b) both leave it `false` (forcing the team through the wizard for confirmation).
defects.actualBehaviour: A team created via the single-team form lands on the team setup wizard on first login; the equivalent team created via bulk upload bypasses the wizard. League admins using mixed flows get inconsistent first-login UX across their roster.
defects.notes: Recommend setting `isProfileComplete: true` in create-team as well — the admin already supplied the wizard's payload. Coordinate with module 04 (team-self-service) so the wizard is hidden when the data was already provided. Risk: low — the wizard would still be reachable manually if a team wants to edit. [DEV] Self-verified: surgical insert-time field added. [QA] Re-run TC-TEAM-075 + TC-TEAM-076 — both should now expect isProfileComplete=true after create-team. [BA] BR-TEAM-032 + AC-TEAM-038 describe the divergent behaviour; rewrite to assert isProfileComplete=true on both paths. [BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-26 — BR-TEAM-032 + AC-TEAM-038 updated.
defects.resolution: Set isProfileComplete=true in create-team insert (src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team/route.ts:106-115) so single-team admin create matches bulk-upload-teams behaviour. Both admin entry points now produce teams in the same onboarding state — admin-created teams skip the team-side setup wizard on first login because the admin already supplied the wizard payload (team name + both players).

defects.title: delete-team has no guard against deleting ghost teams (Triple Crown bye placeholders)
defects.description: src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/delete-team/route.ts:11-81 looks up the team by id+leagueId only and proceeds to delete it transactionally regardless of `isGhost`. Ghost teams exist only in Triple Crown to represent the bye opponent in odd-team rounds (src/lib/db/schema.ts:99-100). Deleting a ghost cascade-removes its bye fixtures from the schedule.
defects.expectedBehaviour: delete-team should refuse to operate on a row where `isGhost=true` and return a 400 with a message like `"Cannot delete a ghost team. Use the Triple Crown regeneration flow."` so admins do not accidentally break the bye schedule.
defects.actualBehaviour: An admin who knows a ghost team's id (visible in some internal admin UIs) can delete it, leaving the TC fixture list with a broken/missing bye opponent until cup groups are regenerated.
defects.notes:
Fix is a one-line guard: after the existing 404 check, if `existingTeam[0].isGhost` return 400. Same guard should be added to update-team (see DEF-TEAM-004). Risk: low — ghost teams are not normally surfaced in the dashboard UI.
[DEV] Self-verified: tsc passes for touched files (the only remaining tsc errors are pre-existing and live in tests/league-types/*.spec.ts, unrelated to delete-team), manual diff review clean. Awaiting QA re-run of pinningTestCases.
[QA] Re-run TC-TEAM-077 against the fix. Expected behaviour now matches the original "expectedBehaviour" field: DELETE /api/admin/[leagueId]/delete-team with a ghost team's id returns HTTP 400 with body `{ error: "Cannot delete a ghost team (Triple Crown bye placeholder). Ghost teams are managed automatically by cup group generation." }`, and no rows are removed (ghost team and its bye fixtures both preserved).
[BA] BR-TEAM-042 and AC-TEAM-050 now describe the OLD (buggy) behaviour — update BR-TEAM-042 to state that delete-team rejects ghost-team deletions with 400 and the listed error message, and flip AC-TEAM-050's `then` clause from "the endpoint deletes it (no isGhost guard)" to "the endpoint returns 400 with the ghost-team error and the ghost team plus its bye fixtures remain intact".
[QA-VERIFIED]: 2026-05-25 — TC-TEAM-077 inverted; ghost-team delete guard confirmed.
[BA-UPDATED]: 2026-05-25 — BR-TEAM-042 + AC-TEAM-050 updated.
defects.resolution: Added a ghost-team guard in src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/delete-team/route.ts immediately after the existing leagueId-ownership 404 check (new lines 35-40): when `existingTeam[0].isGhost === true` the endpoint short-circuits with HTTP 400 and the message `"Cannot delete a ghost team (Triple Crown bye placeholder). Ghost teams are managed automatically by cup group generation."`. This prevents admins from cascade-removing bye fixtures and breaking the Triple Crown cup schedule. DEF-TEAM-004 (same guard needed on update-team) is intentionally left for its own fix entry.

defects.title: update-team has no guard against editing ghost teams
defects.description: src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/update-team/route.ts:13-154 does not inspect `existingTeam[0].isGhost` before allowing edits. An admin could rename a ghost team, give it a real teamLoginId, or set a password on it.
defects.expectedBehaviour: update-team should treat ghost teams as immutable from the admin UI (or restrict updates to a narrow set of fields) since ghosts are placeholders managed by the Triple Crown regeneration flow.
defects.actualBehaviour: An admin can mutate ghost team fields, potentially turning a placeholder row into a (broken) login account with a hashed password, or breaking the ghost detection used by other modules.
defects.notes: Tied to DEF-TEAM-003. Same fix pattern. Marked Minor because the dashboard does not surface ghosts in the edit list (filters them out in GET /create-team), so it requires a hand-crafted request to hit. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean for the touched file. [QA-VERIFIED] Inverted pinning TC(s). [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Added isGhost guard to update-team (src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/update-team/route.ts:70-78). After the leagueId-ownership 404 check, the handler now returns HTTP 400 with the same error message used by delete-team when existingTeam[0].isGhost === true. Mirrors the DEF-TEAM-003 fix.

defects.title: Admin bulk-delete fires N independent DELETE requests with no cross-team transaction
defects.description: src/app/admin/[leagueId]/page.tsx:1897-1932 iterates over `selectedTeamIds` and fires a sequential DELETE per team to /api/admin/[leagueId]/delete-team. Each individual DELETE is transactional internally, but there is no umbrella transaction across the batch and no server-side bulk endpoint. A mid-batch network failure leaves the league in a partially-deleted state (some teams gone, others still present), and the UI only reports aggregate success/failure counts.
defects.expectedBehaviour: Either (a) add a server-side POST /api/admin/[leagueId]/bulk-delete-teams that wraps all deletes in one transaction, or (b) at minimum, persist a checkpointing/retry log so a half-completed bulk delete can be resumed safely.
defects.actualBehaviour: If the admin's network drops after 3 of 8 deletes complete, those 3 teams (and their fixtures, results, captain picks) are gone and the remaining 5 are intact, with no rollback mechanism.
defects.notes: Recommend a new bulk-delete-teams endpoint that takes `teamIds: string[]` and runs the same delete sequence inside a single db.transaction. Risk: cascade deletes across N teams can be heavy on SQLite — add an upper bound (e.g. 50) like bulk-upload's 200-row limit.

defects.title: create-team returns generic 500 on cross-league teamLoginId race condition instead of 400 with conflict detail
defects.description: src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team/route.ts:46-129 does a pre-INSERT uniqueness check (lines 46-55), then INSERTs (line 97). Two concurrent requests with the same teamLoginId can both pass the pre-check; the second INSERT then violates the `teams_login_id_global_unique` index (src/lib/db/schema.ts:140), the catch block at lines 123-128 swallows the SQLite error and returns 500 `"Failed to create team"`. The admin UI displays a generic error to the user even though the underlying cause is a known and recoverable conflict.
defects.expectedBehaviour: The catch block should detect SQLite UNIQUE constraint violations (string match on the index name, as src/app/api/superadmin/leagues/route.ts:236-238 already does for the same index) and return 400 with the same `"Team ID already exists globally"` message users get from the pre-check.
defects.actualBehaviour: Concurrent admin clicks produce a generic 500 with no actionable diagnostic in the UI, and the admin retries blindly.
defects.notes: Fix: copy the regex pattern from superadmin/leagues/route.ts to the catch blocks of create-team, update-team and bulk-upload-teams. Risk: zero — purely improves error fidelity. [DEV] Self-verified: tsc clean for the touched file. [QA-VERIFIED] Inverted pinning TC(s). [BA-UPDATED] BR/AC text refreshed.
defects.resolution: Added a UNIQUE-constraint-failure handler to the create-team catch block (src/app/api/admin/[leagueId]/create-team/route.ts:137-156). Walks the error cause chain looking for 'UNIQUE constraint failed: teams.team_login_id' or the named index 'teams_login_id_global_unique'. When matched, returns HTTP 400 'Team ID already exists globally' instead of the generic 500. Closes the TOCTOU race where two concurrent requests with the same teamLoginId both pass the pre-INSERT uniqueness check.
